name: Pension Haus Elisabeth
beschreibung:
Overview

Haus Elisabeth (also known as Pension Elisabeth) is located in the mountain village of Vent in the rear Ötztal at an altitude of around 1,900 metres. The family-friendly guesthouse is run by Anita Scheiber; the address is Franz-Senn-Weg 1, 6458 Vent. The comfortable rooms, furnished in cosy Tyrolean style, have a private bath/WC or shower/WC, satellite TV and, in most cases, a balcony. Many of the rooms offer a third bed and are therefore well suited to families. In addition, three apartments are available (Type A at 50 square metres, Type B and Type C at 65 square metres each), along with a breakfast room. Vent has only around 160 inhabitants and lies at the end of the Venter Tal, so there is no through traffic in the village.

History/Background

Vent is an almost 800-year-old mountain farming village. Travellers were already coming to the valley in the 18th century, fascinated by the mighty mountains and the glacial lakes. At the end of the 19th century, tourism received its first boost under village priest Senn: he trained mountain guides and had mountain huts built that are still valued by mountain lovers today. According to its own description, Haus Elisabeth is one of the most traditional houses in Vent.

Getting There

Vent lies in the rear Ötztal, around 20 minutes from Sölden. During the day a scheduled bus service runs, which is partly free and offers connections to Sölden and Obergurgl. Many guests arrive by car and park it during their stay, since there is no through traffic in the village itself. In winter, the Stableinbahn is only about 100 metres from the house and can almost always be reached on skis.

Tips

The house serves a breakfast buffet. Children receive a discount of up to 100 percent (up to 2 years), group discounts are available on request, and for short stays of one to two days a surcharge of 10 to 20 percent is charged. For dogs there is a fee of 7 euros per day. For the apartments, a final cleaning fee of 35 euros is added, plus an optional breakfast at 13 euros per person. The prices do not include the tourist tax. Cross-country skiers will find a three-kilometre ski trail into the Rofental, and around the village there are two trails plus a five-kilometre toboggan run.

Best Time to Visit

In winter, Vent is a quiet starting point for skiing: the ski area is right on the doorstep, and the large winter sports resorts of Sölden and Obergurgl are about 20 minutes away. In summer, Vent is suitable for easy family hikes as well as high mountain tours, for example to the Ötzi discovery site or to the Wildspitze, the highest mountain in Tyrol. Both seasons are well suited, depending on whether skiing and cross-country skiing or hiking and mountaineering are the priority.
